code1.cause: One phase (Y) is not reaching the pump properly.
code1.action: Check the Y-phase fuse and wiring at the panel. Call your dealer if it keeps happening.

code2.cause: One of the three phases is missing, so the motor cannot run safely.
code2.action: Check the fuses and the supply. Call an electrician or your dealer.

code3.cause: The supply voltage is too high and can burn the motor.
code3.action: Wait until the supply is normal. Do not restart while it stays high.

code4.cause: The three phase wires are in the wrong order, so the motor turns backwards.
code4.action: Do not run the pump. Ask an electrician to swap any two phase wires.

code5.cause: The pump is running without water.
code5.action: Check the water level and the foot valve. Restart only when water is available.

code6.cause: The cable to the motor is broken or disconnected on all phases.
code6.action: Check the cable and joints from the panel to the motor. Call your dealer.

code7.cause: The cable to the motor is partly broken, or a joint is loose on some phases.
code7.action: Check the cable joints and terminals. Call your dealer.

code8.cause: The motor is taking too much current, from a blocked pump or a weak supply.
code8.action: Check the pump for a blockage. Wait, then restart. Call your dealer if it repeats.

code9.cause: The voltages of the three phases are very different from each other.
code9.action: Wait for the supply to balance. Tell the power company if it continues.

code10.cause: The supply voltage is too low for the motor to run safely.
code10.action: Wait until the voltage improves before starting again.

unknown.cause: The pump found a problem it could not name.
unknown.action: Call your dealer and tell them the problem code.
